#Import Library 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(limma)
library(factoextra)
library(MASS)


Figure_Export <- file.path(here(),"Figures")

Data_Import <- file.path(here(), "Data")
```


#Import Metadata and Matrix Data

```{r}
#Access Metadata
Metadata <- readRDS(file = file.path(Data_Import, "GSE10072_Metadata.rds"))

#Extract specific columns of interest for PCA check
Cols_of_Interest <- Metadata %>% dplyr::select(geo_accession, 
                                               Tissue_Type = source_name_ch1,
                                               Sex = characteristics_ch1,
                                               Smoking_Status = characteristics_ch1.2,
                                               Stage_of_Cancer = characteristics_ch1.3) %>%
  mutate(Stage_and_Tissue_Type = paste(Tissue_Type,"_",Stage_of_Cancer))

Matrix <- readRDS(file = file.path(Data_Import, "GSE10072_Processed_Data.rds"))
```

#Run a PCA to look for potential batch effects or other effects that may distort the analysis

A PCA analysis will be run to look for and identify any potential batch effects or cofounders that might need to be checked. Although other checks can be done as well, the only one performed here is a PCA analysis.
```{r}
#Make PCA Matrix
pca_matrix <- Matrix %>% t()

#Again double check to make sure the sample names in the Matrix and the Metadata are in the same order
identical(rownames(pca_matrix), Metadata$geo_accession)

#Run PCA analysis
PCA <- prcomp(x = pca_matrix, scale = FALSE) #No need for scaling since its already normalized via RMA

#Look at PCA plots

#Faceted by Sex
fviz_pca_biplot(X = PCA,
                geom.var = c(""),
                habillage = Cols_of_Interest$Sex,
                label = "none")

fviz_pca_ind(X = PCA)

fviz_pca_var(X = PCA)

#Faceted by Smoking Status
fviz_pca_biplot(X = PCA,
                geom.var = c(""),
                habillage = Cols_of_Interest$Smoking_Status,
                label = "none")

#Stage of the Tumor in the patient (even if the tissue is non-tumors). Each patient has a normal tissue and adenocarcinoma matched sample, so every normal tissue sample will have the status of the paired tumor.
fviz_pca_biplot(X = PCA,
                geom.var = c(""),
                habillage = Cols_of_Interest$Stage_and_Tissue_Type,
                label = "none")

#Faceted by Tissue Type (and we get results that make sense where normal and cancerous tissue have quite a bit different expression of genes)
fviz_pca_biplot(X = PCA,
                geom.var = c(""),
                habillage = Cols_of_Interest$Tissue_Type,
                label = "none")

ggsave(filename = file.path(Figure_Export, "PCA_GSE10072.png"))

```

#Run the Differential Gene Expression Analysis using Limma

```{r}
#Create a Factor where the reference level will be the normal lung tissue
Cols_of_Interest <- Cols_of_Interest %>%
  mutate(Tissue_Type = factor(Tissue_Type, levels = c("Normal Lung Tissue", "Adenocarcinoma of the Lung")))

#Create a basic design for the limma() function to run
Design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + Cols_of_Interest$Tissue_Type)

#Choose Names that make sense to be the names of each column
valid_names <- make.names(c("Normal Lung Tissue", "Adenocarcinoma of the Lung"))

colnames(Design) <- valid_names

#Run a Linear fit
fit <- lmFit(object = Matrix, design = Design)

#Although there is only one contrast in this example, choose the contrast that will be compared
contrasts <- makeContrasts(Adenocarcinoma.of.the.Lung-Normal.Lung.Tissue, 
                           levels = Design)

#Re-run the linear fit based on the contrasts designed 
fit_final <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts) 
fit_final <- eBayes(fit_final)

#Extract the results
Lung_Tumor_vs_Normal_Tissue <- topTable(fit = fit_final, number = length(rownames(Matrix)), adjust.method = "BH")

#Add Significance to the results

Lung_Tumor_vs_Normal_Tissue <- Lung_Tumor_vs_Normal_Tissue %>%
  mutate(Significance = case_when(
    adj.P.Val < 0.05 & logFC > 1 ~ "Upregulated", #Fold Change of 2 or more
    adj.P.Val < 0.05 & logFC < -1 ~ "Downregulated", #Fold Change of 0.5 or less
    TRUE ~ "No Significance"
  ))

saveRDS(Lung_Tumor_vs_Normal_Tissue, file = file.path(Data_Import, "GSE10072_DEG_results.rds"))

#Make a Table of significance results
significance_table <- table(Lung_Tumor_vs_Normal_Tissue$Significance)

#Make a Graph of the results to duplicate 1C from Xiong et al 2020

Lung_Tumor_vs_Normal_Tissue %>%
ggplot(aes(x=logFC, y = -log10(adj.P.Val)))+
  geom_point(aes(color = Significance))+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed")+
  geom_vline(xintercept = -1, linetype = "dashed")+
  xlim(-5, 5)+
  ylim(0, 50)+
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))+
  labs(title = "GSE10072", x = "log2FoldChange", y = "-log10(adj.pvalue)")+
  #labs(caption = paste0("# of Downregulated Genes: ", Up_or_down[1],", # of No Significance Genes: ", Up_or_down[2],", # of Upregulated Genes: ", Up_or_down[3]))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Downregulated" = "#7CC5D6",
                                "No Significance" = "#2C2E2D",
                                "Upregulated" = "#E74033"))+
annotate("text", x = -3.75, y = 45, size = 3.5, label = paste("Downregulated Genes: ", significance_table [1]))+
annotate("text", x = 3.75, y = 45, size = 3.5, label = paste("Upregulated Genes: ", significance_table [3]))

ggsave(filename = file.path(Figure_Export, "DEG_GSE10072_Fig1C.png"))

```
